facts: Public ihklib.h111+ accepts device index and separate writable output OS index; no device==OS constraint.

Current public specification ihk.tex1310-1345 describes privileged create/configure on dev_index, returnOSindex, reserving resources and assigning them to new OS; no no-existing-OS precondition. Its broad all-OS rollback policy is explicit.

Current C/Rust choreography checks/releases device reserved resources before environment validation, reserves requested free resources, then creates an OS without a no-existing-OS test. Existing assigned resources on OS0 are not those device reserved resources.

SMP backend create allocates a new per-OS object and preserves parent device; it does not reject an occupied OS0. Host allocator uses global first-freeOSslot, stores parent dev_data and returns minor, max64.

Therefore device0 with OS0 occupied and available disjoint resources may create globalOS1 under existing privileged/exclusive serialization contract. This needs no multiple-device or cross-device ABI assumption.
